# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [☝]

I can see a display reading 0, a purple light, and three wires ordered yellow, red, green. Blind’s ☝ gesture has no established meaning yet, so I cannot safely interpret it. I will report all visible facts aloud to both others; Mute can use the manual to establish gesture meanings or send instructions for me to relay.

``` 
speak(text="Visible bomb state: display reads 0. Light is purple. Wires in order: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Blind gestured one symbol, but no code has been established.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 👍 👍 👍 👍 🤝 👍 👍 👍]

The light has changed from purple to yellow while the display and wire order remain unchanged. Mute sent a gesture sequence that appears structurally like five thumbs-up signs, a handshake, then three thumbs-up signs. I cannot know its meaning, but Blind can hear my description and may combine it with Mute’s manual-derived protocol.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Update: light is now yellow; display still 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute gestured: five thumbs-up signs, then a handshake, then three thumbs-up signs.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the light changed from purple to yellow. I described your gesture sequence aloud to Blind exactly as five thumbs-up, handshake, three thumbs-up.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [🖐 🤝 🤟]

The only visible change is that the light is now red; the display remains 0 and the wire order remains yellow, red, green. Mute’s new gesture sequence is open hand, handshake, then the three-finger sign. I will relay it exactly to Blind rather than guessing its encoding.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Current visible state: display 0; light red; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. Mute's latest gesture sequence: open hand 🖐, handshake 🤝, three-finger sign 🤟.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your latest gesture sequence and the red-light update to Blind.")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light is now green, with display still 0 and wires still ordered yellow, red, green. No new gesture arrived. I should announce this state change to both; Blind may be tracking the sequence of light colours, while Mute can determine the required action from the manual.

``` 
speak(text="Visible state update: display remains 0; wires remain 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now green.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The display remains 0 and the wires remain yellow, red, green in positions 1–3. The light has changed to white, extending the observed colour sequence. I will report this immediately.

``` 
speak(text="Visible update: display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now white.")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light is now orange. The display remains 0, and the wire order is still 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I will report the updated state and preserve the observed light sequence for the others.

``` 
speak(text="Visible update: display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now orange. Light sequence observed so far: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange.")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The light has changed to blue; the display remains 0 and the wires are still yellow, red, green in positions 1 through 3. The full observed sequence is now purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. I will relay that exact update.

``` 
speak(text="Visible update: display 0; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green; light is now blue. Sequence: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue.")
```

TURN 8
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

The light has returned to purple after the sequence purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue, suggesting a repeating seven-colour cycle. The display remains 0 and wires remain yellow, red, green. Mute’s single thumbs-up gesture should be relayed exactly to Blind, without assuming it means an action.

``` 
speak(to="blind", text="Visible state: display 0; light purple; wires 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. The colour cycle has returned to purple after purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange, blue. Mute just gestured one thumbs-up: 👍.")
speak(to="mute", text="I relayed your single thumbs-up gesture to Blind. The visible light has returned to purple.")
```
